family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Shift every alphabetic character in a string by a given integer number of positions in the alphabet, wrapping around from z to a (or Z to A). The shift amount may be negative or larger than 26. Non-alphabetic characters are left unchanged, and the case of each letter is preserved.
hidden_tests: assert caesar_shift('The Quick Fox', 7) == 'Aol Xbpjr Mve'

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Apply the ROT13 substitution cipher to a string: rotate every alphabetic character 13 positions through the alphabet, preserving case, and leave all non-alphabetic characters unchanged.
hidden_tests: assert rot13('The Quick Brown Fox') == 'Gur Dhvpx Oebja Sbk'
assert rot13('Attack at Dawn!') == 'Nggnpx ng Qnja!'

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Apply the Atbash cipher to a string, which maps 'a' to 'z', 'b' to 'y', and so on for each letter of the alphabet, preserving the case of each letter. Non-alphabetic characters must remain unchanged and in the same position.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Encode a string using run-length encoding: replace each maximal run of consecutive identical characters with the character followed by the count of repetitions (e.g. 'aaab' becomes 'a3b1'). An empty string encodes to an empty string.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Decode a run-length encoded string where each character is followed by a positive integer count (e.g. 'a3b1' becomes 'aaab'). Counts may be more than one digit long. An empty string decodes to an empty string.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Count how many vowel characters (a, e, i, o, u), in either uppercase or lowercase, appear in a string. Non-vowel characters, including consonants, digits, and punctuation, are not counted.
reference:
def count_vowels(s):
    return sum(1 for ch in s if ch.lower() in "aeiou")

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Count how many consonant letters (alphabetic characters that are not a, e, i, o, or u), in either uppercase or lowercase, appear in a string. Digits, punctuation, whitespace, and vowels are not counted.
reference:
def count_consonants(s):
    return sum(1 for ch in s if ch.isalpha() and ch.lower() not in "aeiou")

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Return a copy of the input string with every vowel character (a, e, i, o, u), in either uppercase or lowercase, removed. All other characters keep their original order and position relative to each other.
hidden_tests: assert remove_vowels('The Quick Fox') == 'Th Qck Fx'
reference:
def remove_vowels(s):
    return ''.join(ch for ch in s if ch.lower() not in "aeiou")

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Count how many uppercase alphabetic characters appear in a string. Lowercase letters, digits, whitespace, and punctuation are not counted.
reference:
def count_uppercase(s):
    return sum(1 for ch in s if ch.isupper())

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Count how many lowercase alphabetic characters appear in a string. Uppercase letters, digits, whitespace, and punctuation are not counted.
reference:
def count_lowercase(s):
    return sum(1 for ch in s if ch.islower())

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Count how many numeric digit characters (0-9) appear in a string. Letters, whitespace, and punctuation are not counted.
reference:
def count_digits(s):
    return sum(1 for ch in s if ch.isdigit())

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Return a copy of the string with the case of every alphabetic character swapped: uppercase letters become lowercase and lowercase letters become uppercase. Non-alphabetic characters remain unchanged.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Count the number of whitespace-separated words in a string, treating any run of spaces, tabs, or newlines as a single separator. Leading, trailing, and repeated whitespace must not affect the count, and an empty or whitespace-only string has zero words.
hidden_tests: assert count_words('this is a longer sentence here') == 6
assert count_words('just one more test case here') == 6
reference:
def count_words(s):
    return len(s.split())

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string of whitespace-separated words, return the longest word. If several words share the maximum length, return the one that appears first in the string. An empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty string.
hidden_tests: assert longest_word('one two three four five six') == 'three'
assert longest_word('z zz zzz zz z') == 'zzz'
assert longest_word('brevity is the soul of wit') == 'brevity'

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string of whitespace-separated words, return the shortest word. If several words share the minimum length, return the one that appears first in the string. An empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty string.
hidden_tests: assert shortest_word('one two three four five six') == 'one'
assert shortest_word('brevity is the soul of wit') == 'is'

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string of whitespace-separated words, find the word (case-insensitive) that occurs the most times. If multiple words are tied for the highest count, return whichever of them appears first in the string. Return the word in lowercase. An empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty string.
visible_tests: assert most_common_word('the cat sat on the mat') == 'the'
hidden_tests: assert most_common_word('dog cat dog cat bird') == 'dog'
assert most_common_word('a b c a b a') == 'a'
assert most_common_word('hello world hello world hello') == 'hello'
assert most_common_word('z z y y x') == 'z'
assert most_common_word('single occurrence each here now') == 'single'
assert most_common_word('apple banana apple cherry banana apple') == 'apple'

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string, reverse the characters within each single-space-separated word while keeping the words in their original order. Words remain separated by single spaces in the output.
visible_tests: assert reverse_each_word('a bb ccc') == 'a bb ccc'
hidden_tests: assert reverse_each_word('a b c') == 'a b c'
assert reverse_each_word('one two three four') == 'eno owt eerht ruof'
assert reverse_each_word('aa bb cc dd') == 'aa bb cc dd'
assert reverse_each_word('keep it simple') == 'peek ti elpmis'
reference:
def reverse_each_word(s):
    return ' '.join(w[::-1] for w in s.split(' '))

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string of whitespace-separated words, return a new string with the words in reverse order but each word itself left unchanged. Multiple spaces between words collapse to a single space in the output, and leading/trailing whitespace is ignored.
visible_tests: assert reverse_word_order('one two three') == 'three two one'
assert reverse_word_order('a b c d') == 'd c b a'
hidden_tests: assert reverse_word_order('the quick brown fox jumps') == 'jumps fox brown quick the'
assert reverse_word_order('multiple   spaces   here') == 'here spaces multiple'
assert reverse_word_order('word1 word2 word3 word4 word5') == 'word5 word4 word3 word2 word1'
assert reverse_word_order('z y x w v') == 'v w x y z'
assert reverse_word_order('keep it simple stupid') == 'stupid simple it keep'
reference:
def reverse_word_order(s):
    return ' '.join(reversed(s.split()))

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Convert a string to sentence case: make every letter lowercase, then capitalize the first alphabetic character found in the string (if any). If the string contains no alphabetic characters, return it fully lowercased and otherwise unchanged.
visible_tests: assert sentence_case('the Quick Fox') == 'The quick fox'
hidden_tests: assert sentence_case('   spaced OUT   ') == '   Spaced out   '
assert sentence_case('MULTIPLE. SENTENCES. HERE.') == 'Multiple. sentences. here.'
assert sentence_case('mIxEd CaSe TeXt') == 'Mixed case text'
assert sentence_case('  UPPER first') == '  Upper first'
assert sentence_case('no letters here 123456') == 'No letters here 123456'
assert sentence_case('wELCOME to the JUNGLE') == 'Welcome to the jungle'

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Collapse every maximal run of consecutive identical characters in a string down to a single occurrence of that character (e.g. 'aaabbbcc' becomes 'abc'). An empty string returns an empty string.
